claims.text: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite aboard a Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) on September 4.
The GSLV placed EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit 18 minutes after lifting off from Sriharikota at 2.55 a.m. on September 4.
EOS-05 is India's first imaging satellite designed to monitor Earth from a geosynchronous orbit approximately 36,000 km high.
ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan stated that EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite ever launched by a GSLV rocket, weighing 2,367 kg.
EOS-05 replaces the EOS-03 mission, which failed in August 2021 due to a cryogenic upper stage ignition anomaly.
ISRO had not conducted any launch missions since the failure of the PSLV-C62 mission on January 12, 2026.
The GSLV-F17 rocket is 51.7 metres tall and has a liftoff mass of 420.5 tonnes.
ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan announced that ISRO plans six more launches in the current financial year, including navigation satellite NVS-03 and the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission.
India had 21 operational Earth observation satellites as of February 2026.
The GSLV-F17 rocket lifted off following a 27.5-hour countdown from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
The EOS-05 satellite is also designated as Gisat-1A.
EOS-05 carries two multispectral imagers, including one with a spatial resolution of 42 metres per pixel.
Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated in Kyiv that India is ready to extend any help in any manner to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
S. Jaishankar stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek that endless war must give way to the end of war.
S. Jaishankar met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during his visit to Kyiv.
An Indian national was killed in an attack in Kyiv two days prior to S. Jaishankar's visit.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia launched jet-powered Shahed drones over Kyiv during Jaishankar's visit.
S. Jaishankar rejected Western claims that buying Russian oil bankrolls the war, stating India's energy sourcing is based on securing supplies for its 1.4 billion people.
S. Jaishankar invited Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha to visit India.
Russian attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea have caused the deaths of five Indian seafarers.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the Shahed drones launched by Russia were built with assistance from Iran.
The Bharatiya Janata Party accused the Congress party of using flawed calculations to convert India's 7.8% GDP growth figure into an imaginary 2.6%.
BJP chief spokesperson Anil Baluni stated that India has revised its GDP base year nine times since Independence.
World Bank executive director Neelkanth Mishra defended India's 7.8% Q1 GDP growth figure, dismissing claims of data manipulation as egregiously wrong.
Former Indian finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg argued that Q1 GDP growth would be 2.6% in nominal terms without the downward revision of the previous year's base figure.
India revised its GDP calculation base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23 in February 2026.
Credit rating agency JCR upgraded India's sovereign rating from 'BBB+' to 'A-' with a stable outlook.
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation reported that India's manufacturing sector grew 9.2% in the April-June quarter of FY 2026-27.
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh claimed that GDP estimates across four years since 2022-23 were revised downwards by a total of 43 lakh crore rupees.
Sanjeev Sanyal, a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council, denied allegations of GDP data manipulation.
Union Minister Kiren Rijiju shared a video of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang praising India's IT growth and AI focus amid the GDP controversy.
